subject: Quantify p95/p99 gap vs hyperscaler — A/B bench plan and asks
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reid <alex.reid@hypercloud.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Nov 2029 15:20:00 +0000
Subject: Quantify p95/p99 gap vs hyperscaler — next steps from today's call

Alex — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we schedule bench runs: 

Summary from discovery:
- You saw a consistent p95 delta of ~60–80ms when comparing your hyperscaler endpoint (their managed endpoint) vs your internal lab results on equivalent models.
- Throughput numbers you shared: ~420 tokens/sec at 8 concurrent connections for the hyperscaler baseline; tails (p99) spike noticeably under 16+ concurrency.
- Primary ask: see a head-to-head A/B run that captures p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens for both endpoints under an agreed load profile.

Proposed A/B bench plan (short):
1) Two variants: HyperCloud managed endpoint (their current production config) vs Redwood inference (dedicated config we propose).
2) Workload profile: mixed requests — 60% short (<64 tokens), 30% medium (64–256 tokens), 10% long (256–1024 tokens). Sequence-length distribution matches your production traces.
3) Concurrency sweep: 1, 4, 8, 16, 32 connections; 10 minute steady-state per step.
4) Metrics to collect: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, median and 95th CPU/GPU utilization, tail error rate.
5) Environment: quantized int8 and fp16 comparator runs (two passes), KV cache enabled vs disabled.
6) Cost calc: token pricing, instance amortization, and estimated egress; produce $/1M tokens.

Ask from you to proceed:
- Confirm the production trace sample (you can share a 30k-request anonymized sample) or confirm the distribution above.
- Share any gating constraints (e.g., run window, IP allowlist) and the hyperscaler endpoint URL and expected auth.

I attached the small CSV you mentioned in the call as a starting reference and a skeleton Redwood run spec. If that plan looks good I'll book a 90-minute bench kickoff and loop Priyom and Marcus for the run scheduling.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
[attachment: current_latency_report.csv (csv)]

Thanks Rishi — that recap is perfect and aligns with what our infra team found. A few clarifications: 

- I'll drop a sanitized sample trace (30k rows) into the Drive link you shared by EOD. Distribution should roughly match your workload proposal.
- Baseline numbers we reported were from their managed endpoint with fp16 weights; we can request an int8 run but expect worse latency due to batching behavior.
- For auth we'll give you a read-only service key for the test endpoints and an IP allowlist window (UTC 2029-11-12 02:00–10:00). Can you run during that window?
- Cost calc: include network egress from their region (us-west) — that matters for our finance team.

Also attaching the CSV we referenced for clarity. If possible, include p99 broken down by request size (short/medium/long).

Alex

Subject: Re: Quantify p95/p99 gap vs hyperscaler — next steps from today's call

Appreciate the quick turn, Alex — we'll run in the allowlist window on 2029-11-12 (we can also do a dry run earlier if you prefer). A couple of operational details and commitments from our side: 

Operational commitments:
- Priyom will orchestrate the A/B runs and provide raw exports of latency histograms and token throughput.
- Marcus will produce a detailed cost model per 1M tokens (separate line items: inference CPU/GPU, memory, egress).
- Grace will build a temporary dashboard (p50/p90/p95/p99 by request-size) and an alerts sheet for unexpected tail behavior.

Deliverables after run (within 48 hours):
- CSV with per-request latencies, aggregated histograms, and tokens/sec by step.
- Short one-page summary with key deltas, root-cause hypotheses for any tail gaps, and recommended options (batching tuning, KV cache, quant profile).
- Estimated cost delta at your requested usage bucket (you told us ~120M tokens/month).

One ask for engineering: please confirm the sequence-length bins you want for the p99 breakout (we propose: short 0–64, medium 65–256, long 257–1024). Priyom: can you also include a run where we artificially spike 5% of requests to 2048 tokens to see tail effects?

If that all looks good I'll upload the Redwood run spec (redwood-ab-plan.yml) and schedule the kickoff at 2029-11-11 16:00 UTC to align on auth and guardrails.

Thanks — looping Priyom/Marcus/Grace to confirm capacity.

— Rishi

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Cc: Alex Reid <alex.reid@hypercloud.com>
Date: Sat, 9 Nov 2029 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: FW: Quantify p95/p99 gap vs hyperscaler — run assignments and checklist

Forwarding Alex's approvals and Rishi's plan — internal action items and owners below. Quoted original for context.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Priyom: set up bench harness with two endpoints (HyperCloud URL + Redwood dedicated pool). Run profile: concurrency sweep [1,4,8,16,32], distribution 60/30/10, int8 + fp16 passes, 10min steady-state per step. ETA: dry run 2029-11-10, full run 2029-11-12 per allowlist.
- Marcus: produce cost model (breakdown + $/1M tokens + sensitivity to batch sizes). ETA: preliminary numbers 2029-11-11 COB.
- Grace: create Grafana temp dashboard (p50/p90/p95/p99 by short/medium/long) + Slack alert channel. ETA: 2029-11-11 morning.
- Rishi: coordinate HubSpot update and share the read-only service key once Alex drops it. ETA: 2029-11-10.

Bench notes / hypotheses to test:
- Hypothesis A: p95 gap is primarily due to batching policy differences on the hyperscaler side (aggressive batching increases tail). We'll run with Redwood continuous batching tuned to your latency SLO and a small max-batch window.
- Hypothesis B: KV cache differences for repeated prefix tokens — test with cache on/off.
- Hypothesis C: Quantization profile — int8 can reduce cost but may increase latency variance; run both.

Attachments: redwood-ab-plan.yml (skeleton run spec) and the CSV Alex provided.

I'll start the dry run tomorrow; will post logs to the Drive folder and ping Alex once we have smoke results.

— Priyom
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
